subject: Post-call: rerank integration & acceptance criteria (SolisHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@solishealth.com>, Priya Ramanathan <priya@solishealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: rerank integration & acceptance criteria (SolisHealth)

Thanks for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on integration approach and the evaluation criteria you asked about.

Recap (30-minute discovery):
- Goal: improve search relevance for clinician-facing content and surface the most clinically-relevant notes for triage workflows.
- Current infra: SolisHealth search index (Elasticsearch) + an embeddings pipeline for semantic search; currently using cosine on embeddings for recall, then simple lexical scoring for ranking.
- Key asks: a) how to wire in Redwood as a reranker, b) auth and routing requirements for production, c) clear eval metrics and baseline comparison, d) expected latency/cost tradeoffs.

Immediate asks from our side (so we can draft the eval runbook):
1) Share a ~500–1,000 sample query->candidate set CSV (preferably anonymized). We attached a template (reranker-eval-template.csv).
2) Confirm whether PII/anonymization constraints require on-prem (you mentioned some workloads may be restricted).
3) Any service-level requirements for p50/p95 latency for the reranker.

Proposed integration patterns (high-level):
- Option A (server-side rerank): send candidate set from your app to Redwood Ranking API; Redwood returns scores + structured outputs; lower client complexity, easier to control model variants at routing layer.
- Option B (client-side cross-encoder): compute embeddings on your side, call Redwood’s cross-encoder endpoint for pairwise scoring (good if you want tight control over batching and to avoid shipping all candidate text).

Initial acceptance criteria we suggest for the pilot:
- Evaluation metrics: MRR@10, NDCG@10, Precision@5 and Recall@100 (we recommend keeping both ranking and retrieval metrics).
- Target: >=0.15 absolute MRR improvement vs. your current embedding baseline (adjustable after sanity check).
- Performance budget: reranker p50 latency <150ms (model dependent) and p95 <400ms for the canonical query set.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (SDK quickstart + example Ranking API calls), reranker-eval-template.csv (CSV template for queries + candidates).

Next steps / timeline:
- Alex: share anonymized sample CSV by EOD Wed (1/14).
- Redwood (Karthik/Soojin): provide a short integration plan + suggested model variants and TopK defaults by Thurs (1/15).
- Run pilot eval across our staging cluster (2 weeks) -> produce MRR/NDCG report + latency/cost estimates.

If you’re good with this, I’ll loop in solutions engineering to create a canary plan and slot a short integration call (~30 min) for early next week.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

--

- reranker-eval-template.csv (csv template, header: query_id,query_text,candidate_id,candidate_text,baseline_score,ground_truth_label)

Thanks Alex — quick technical notes that will help your ML lead sketch the eval: 

Integration patterns (practical notes):
- Server-side rerank (recommended pilot): your service sends candidate payload (IDs + text snippets) to Redwood Ranking API (POST /v1/rank). We handle batching and return scores + optional structured JSON extras (reasoning tokens, confidence). Advantages: single RPC, easier rollout control, and Redwood can apply KV cache for repeated prefixes.
- Client-side scoring (optional): if you want to avoid shipping raw candidate text, compute embeddings on your side and call our cross-encoder with pairwise batches; this reduces data egress but increases client CPU.

Auth & routing: 
- Hosted: API keys for initial pilot; we recommend scoped service keys and short-lived session tokens.
- Dedicated/Private: support for JWT + KMS-backed signing; routing uses metadata tags (region, model_variant). Example header: X-Redwood-Routing: model=rerank-v2,region=us-west

TopK / candidate sizing guidance: 
- For your candidate sizes (50–200), start with TopK=50 for the reranker scoring window, then evaluate precision@5/10. If latency is tight, use a two-stage approach: embeddings recall @100 then rerank top 50 with cross-encoder.

Suggested baseline metrics for the pilot (we’ll produce code snippets to compute these):
- MRR@10 (primary), NDCG@10, Precision@5, Recall@100, and optionally MAP@100.
- Track runtime metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, and cost per 1k queries.

Quick example Ranking API call (pseudo):
POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rank
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <api_key>, X-Redwood-Routing: model=rerank-crossencoder-v1;region=us-west
Body: {"query_id":"q_123","query_text":"short clinical note","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"..."},...],"top_k":50}

We can supply a small SDK snippet (Python/Node) as part of the quickstart to show integration points for auth/routing and structured outputs (tool-calling style JSON).

I’ll attach a short integration checklist and we can map owners/dates after you share the sample CSV.

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
